given: a SKU identifier that has no stock records at any location (the only observable ground for absence, since stock_records is the sole data store and no separate SKU registry exists to distinguish a known-but-empty SKU from an unknown one)
when: the warehouse team member requests that SKU's detail view
then: an explicit "No stock for this SKU" state is shown instead of a blank page or a null error

independence.rationale: AC1-AC3 concern a SKU that has stock rows and its optional detail; AC4 concerns the disjoint case of zero matching stock rows, asserting an explicit empty state grounded in observable data (no rows) rather than a blank page or crash. It replaces the earlier contradictory known-vs-unknown (200-vs-404) split, which is not implementable without a SKU registry table that the architecture does not declare. This empty state can be missing while populated SKUs render correctly, so it fails independently.

architectural_notes: E2E: the zero-rows branch of the SKU-detail read path, React SPA (client/) -> boundary (app/routes/, renders_via react, JSON only) -> service (app/services/) -> repository (app/repositories/) query of stock_records filtered by sku. Because stock_records is the sole data store and NO separate skus/catalog table is declared (see architecture.json persistence_invariants), absence is observable ONLY as zero matching rows; the service therefore treats an empty result as a single, well-defined "no stock for this SKU" state and the boundary returns an empty JSON collection (200), never a 404 that would require a registry to ground. The React component maps empty -> the explicit "No stock for this SKU" state. This deliberately collapses the earlier contradictory known-vs-unknown 200/404 split, which was unimplementable without a SKU registry the architecture does not (and per this revision, need not) add. Cross-cutting: empty-is-a-valid-state (not an error) decided in the service, message rendering owned by the client. Verified real-branch (NFR-F1-4): with no rows seeded for a sku, assert the "No stock for this SKU" state renders instead of a blank page or a null crash.
